text: {"overall_winner": "B", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay B organizes points into clear body paragraphs with topic sentences like 'Having driverless cars can be dangerous' and 'Not only are these cars dangerous; they will cause problems.'", "quality": "Organizational structure", "description": "The essay uses distinct paragraphs each devoted to a single supporting point, giving the argument a clear, logical progression."}, {"evidence": "Essay B integrates quoted evidence from the article, such as 'the technology fails and some is injured, who is at fault-the driver or the manufactuer?' and 'when the vehicle is in danger of backing into an object.'", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay directly quotes and incorporates specific details from the source article to support each of its claims."}, {"evidence": "Essay B opens with a rhetorical question and a clear thesis stating three reasons, then returns to them throughout the body.", "quality": "Thesis-driven argumentation", "description": "The essay announces its position and supporting reasons up front and develops each one in turn, keeping the argument focused."}, {"evidence": "Essay B's conclusion weighs the opposing view ('having driverless cars sounds pretty cool') before reaffirming its position.", "quality": "Acknowledgment of counterargument", "description": "The essay briefly concedes the appeal of driverless cars before restating why the risks outweigh the benefits, strengthening the persuasiveness of the argument."}, {"evidence": "Essay A contains spelling and grammar errors such as 'I belive,' 'paragragh,' 'occured,' 'wouldnt,' 'stilll,' and 'ceases to explain the bad side.'", "quality": "Conventional mechanics", "description": "Essay B is written with noticeably fewer spelling and usage errors, making it more readable and credible than Essay A."}]}
